_comment: tokens.json for Example Brand. W3C Design Tokens spec. ALIGNED to the v3 EDITORIAL RESTRAINT direction so the pack carries ONE visual language. AUTHORITY: this file is NOT the source of truth — colors_and_type.css is the live value layer every page, exemplar and downstream consumer reads. This is a W3C-shaped export of the same system. Aligned on the axes the direction covers (colour, typography, type scale, spacing, layout, radius, surfaces, shadows, strokes); left as authored on the axes it does not (motion, z-index, breakpoints). Theme model: LIGHT-FIRST, EDITORIAL. Dark surfaces exist and are governed - permitted for a hero, closing band, footer, immersive or full-bleed media moment, product reveal or narrative transition, at most two per page. Dark is a compositional device, NOT a theme; there is nothing to switch to. (Was "LIGHT ONLY" - retired 2026-07-30, DR-28.) COLOUR VALUES ARE CANONICAL AND IMMUTABLE as of 2026-07-30; this file is an export and moves in lockstep with the other three token files - every value change is a four-file change.

color._comment: CANONICAL COLOUR FOUNDATION, permanently authored 2026-07-30. These values are canonical and immutable: never modified, interpolated, approximated, replaced or regenerated. Four accents each with one job, used sparingly, plus a warm 16-step neutral canvas. The interface is ~90-95% neutral and ~5% accent as a PAGE aggregate, not a per-section rule. Hierarchy comes from typography, spacing and composition rather than colour: colour reinforces hierarchy, it never creates it, and it never establishes a component's identity. Consume in order: semantic tokens, then canonical tonal steps (only when building a semantic token), then legacy aliases (compatibility only). Governance: governance/website/foundation/COLOUR.md, rulebooks/visual-language.md section 15, component-governance/COMPOSE.md section C.5. Decisions: DECISION-REGISTER.md DR-23 to DR-34.

font._comment: ONE typeface for the whole experience. Manrope is retired — it was never vendored in this pack.

instrument-sans.$description: The single family — display, body and editorial roles all resolve here. Vendored as a variable font across the 400–700 weight range (SIL OFL).

manrope.$description: DEPRECATED alias — re-pointed to Instrument Sans. The system uses a single typeface.

inter.$description: DEPRECATED alias — re-pointed to Instrument Sans. The system uses a single typeface.

typography._comment: Major Third modular scale, ratio 1.25, from a 20px base, every calculated size rounded to the nearest 4px. The TABLE is normative: chaining the ratio would put the top step at 76; the authored scale says 72. Do not recompute. Every heading level inherits -0.04em tracking and 120% leading; body and supporting text take 145%.

supporting.$description: Supporting Text — eyebrows, captions, labels, metadata, supporting UI text. ONE step for all five. Secondary text colour. 20 ÷ 1.25 = 16, so it is the scale's own next step down.

body.$description: P — default paragraph copy. Secondary text colour.

h6.$description: H6 — smallest heading level. Primary text colour.

h2.$description: H2 — section headlines across the page.

h1.$description: H1 — the page's commanding headline. Also the size a large metric figure takes; there is no off-scale display size.

eyebrow.$description: DEPRECATED name — re-pointed to Supporting Text. Editorial, not tracked-out uppercase.

caption.$description: DEPRECATED name — re-pointed to Supporting Text.

body-sm.$description: DEPRECATED name — re-pointed to Supporting Text.

body-lg.$description: DEPRECATED name — re-pointed to P. The scale has one body size.

body-emphasis.$description: Body emphasis — inline emphasis and key phrases at the body size.

spacing._comment: Three NAMED steps carry the language — XS, M, XL. They are aliases of steps that already exist on the 4px grid below; there is no second scale. The grid is what any component-specific override is drawn from.

xs.$description: XS — between tightly related UI elements: label→value, icon→text, metadata groups.

m.$description: M — default spacing between related content groups: heading→body, body→CTA, card title→description.

xl.$description: XL — between major visual groups: heading group→primary content (placeholder, screenshot, dashboard).

rhythm-opening.$description: SECTION RHYTHM — marker → heading. The section's opening gesture. The marker introduces the section; the heading begins the narrative; those are two moments and must not read as attached. THE RULE IS THE ORDER, NOT THE NUMBER: opening > content > cluster, at every viewport.

rhythm-cluster.$description: SECTION RHYTHM — heading → supporting copy. The heading and its supporting copy are ONE thought; do not insert intermediate spacing inside the cluster.

rhythm-content.$description: SECTION RHYTHM — heading cluster → primary content. The hand-off from the argument to what carries it.

creative._comment: CREATIVE-FIRST COMPOSITION (rulebooks/creatives.md): creative assets are first-class compositional elements. Their proportion, measure and placement are determined BEFORE the surrounding layout. Layout adapts to the creative; the creative never adapts to available space. A creative has three properties and governing only one governs nothing — the same approved ratio at 90% and at 35% of a composition are different decisions, and the same ratio at the same size can still be assembled media-first or text-first at random. Three closed vocabularies follow. A placeholder inherits all three: it represents the FUTURE CREATIVE, never the available space.

ratio._comment: PROPORTION — the four approved ratios, and only these four. Never invent a ratio whose only purpose is filling available space. If a layout cannot accommodate an approved ratio, the LAYOUT changes.

square.$description: 1:1 — product fragments, supporting editorial visuals, icons presented as imagery, small creative moments.

portrait.$description: 3:4 — portrait photography, editorial photography, human subjects, storytelling imagery.

landscape.$description: 4:3 — editorial illustrations, product compositions, medium-emphasis creatives, general visual storytelling.

wide.$description: 16:9 — product interfaces, dashboards, platform screenshots, wide editorial imagery, hero demonstrations.

presence._comment: PRESENCE — how much compositional AUTHORITY the creative holds, as a share of the composition. Deliberately not 'scale': a creative at 70% is not merely larger, it is dominant; at 25% it is supporting. Expressed as a share so it stays responsive and comparable across sections, and so it maps onto the existing focal-weight model instead of inventing a second notion of importance. Deliberately not 'dominance' either — that term is already load-bearing in VISUAL_LANGUAGE with its own failure modes, and a creative is often not the dominant element.

xs.$description: Incidental — a fragment beside the argument.

l.$description: Leading — the creative carries the section.

xl.$description: Dominant — the creative IS the section.

anchor._comment: PLACEMENT — where the creative sits and how content relates to it. Without this, a governed ratio at a governed presence can still be assembled text-then-media, media-then-text or interleaved at random. Anchoring is what makes creative placement deterministic. The values are the vocabulary; each is realized as a .cr-anchor-* class in colors_and_type.css.
anchor.$value: left | right | inline | bleed | framed | floating | inset
anchor.$description: The seven approved anchors. 'framed' is the bracketed media container the pack already ships; 'bleed' runs the creative edge to edge; 'inset' holds it within the editorial measure.

environment._comment: ENVIRONMENTAL IMAGERY — the canonical library (ASSETS.md). Approved environmental creative, delivered by people and vendored into the pack. A section SELECTS one by name; there is deliberately no handle that accepts a URL, because a path typed at a call site can point at a stock library, a generated image or a file outside the pack, and every one of those reads as a legitimate CSS value. Naming the library makes "use an approved asset" a property of the mechanism rather than a rule someone has to remember. Each entry binds its asset to a MEASURED FOCUS: every master is 3:2, so all four approved ratios crop it, and a centre crop is simply the crop nobody chose. The focus values were checked against the crop each produces at all four ratios, not picked by eye from the full frame. The creative itself is never modified — atmosphere is built above it in CSS, from the surface treatment and the scrim. The pool is entirely LANDSCAPE at source: it serves 16:9, 4:3 and 1:1 naturally, and 3:4 only through a deliberate focus.

cliffside-muted.$description: Muted, near-monochrome cliff and forest under a white sky — the most restrained member; the environment recedes furthest behind copy. Focus 50% 42% — the point the cover-crop preserves.

dawn-haze.$description: Backlit morning haze, flare left, silhouetted treeline right, still water — the most cinematic; large natural negative space on the light side. Focus 55% 50% — the point the cover-crop preserves.

lake-mirror.$description: Symmetrical mirror lake under cumulus — bright and calm, but deliberately centred, so it is a quiet closing surface rather than a hero. Focus 50% 50% — the point the cover-crop preserves.

massif-banded.$description: Grey massif, dark conifer band, turquoise lake — strong horizontal depth layers; holds its subject at every approved ratio. Focus 40% 45% — the point the cover-crop preserves.

massif-clear.$description: Jagged limestone massif over transparent shallows — the most detailed; nearly 4:3 at source (1.328). Focus 50% 42% — the point the cover-crop preserves.

ridges-distant.$description: Receding hazy ridges under a deep cloud bank — the largest quiet sky in the library; the most versatile across ratios. Focus 50% 50% — the point the cover-crop preserves.

valley-deep.$description: Enclosed green valley flanked by forest, glacier peak beyond — the deepest recession; saturated and dense at the edges. Focus 64% 45% — the point the cover-crop preserves.

marker._comment: The Section Marker is part of the Example Brand visual identity: two hard-cornered squares, one at each edge of the section's content width, appearing once at the beginning of a major section. It aligns to the content well's inner edge — never the section's outer edge — because its job is establishing the page's horizontal alignment. It takes the accent assigned to the section, never a text colour.

size.$description: Both width and height of each square.

radius.$description: Hard corners. The marker is the one element in the system with no radius.

radius._comment: The Example Brand website CURRENTLY STANDARDIZES ON two radii: control 6px (buttons, inputs, chips) and large surface 12px (cards, panels). The wider vocabulary stays defined so a future component can reach for it with an explicit justification — but nothing in the current language may introduce a third value by drift. The former signature pill is retired from buttons.

full.$description: Genuinely circular or lozenge affordances only — avatars, circular icons. NOT buttons.

buttons.$description: Button radius — the control radius. The former full-pill signature is retired by the direction.

pills.$description: Badge and tag radius where a genuine lozenge is required.

icons.$description: Icon background radius — the control radius.

images.$description: Image and placeholder radius — matches cards.

shadow._comment: NOT USED BY THE CURRENT VISUAL LANGUAGE. Shadows are used nowhere throughout the website; hierarchy is achieved using spacing, typography, alignment and composition. These tokens are DEPRECATED and retained as `none` rather than removed, so any consumer still referencing them renders correctly flat instead of breaking. The prohibition itself is a rule — see rulebooks/visual-language.md §12.

surface._comment: Canonical surface tier. The hierarchy is INVERTED from a conventional white-page system: the page ground is surface-4 (the warm field) and surface-1 (white) is an ELEVATION on top of it. Measured across every approved reference frame, #F6F5EF is the dominant field (55/23/66/36/63/80 percent of pixels) and white appears as raised cards (10-13 percent). DR-26. The previous 0-indexed numbering collided with this name-for-name and is deprecated: old 0 -> surface-4, old 1 (#EFEEE7) -> surface-5, old 2 and 3 -> surface-1.

1.$description: Elevation: cards and raised panels on the page ground.

4.$description: THE PAGE GROUND - the canonical default page surface. Canonical, not mandatory: a section may declare another approved background, and the page ground exists only beneath those that have not.

0.$description: DEPRECATED -> surface-4. Retained because nothing in this pack is deleted.

accent.$description: The accent band surface. Takes primary ink (6.36:1), never white (2.26:1).

dark.$description: Governed editorial dark surface. NOT a theme - a compositional device, permitted for a hero, closing band, footer, immersive or full-bleed media moment, product reveal or narrative transition, AT MOST TWO PER PAGE. DR-28.

texture._comment: Surface treatment — the MATERIAL a branded surface is made of. Not decoration and not depth. Three shared CANONICAL Brand Pack assets, composited in one fixed order (noise → film → grunge-retro → base surface; the FILM layer is applied to PHOTOGRAPHIC BASES ONLY — a solid colour has no tone for it to vary, so over a flat field it reads as dirt on the block rather than as material) to soften the digital precision of a large branded surface and give it a tactile, printed, editorial character. Do not replace, regenerate or substitute the assets without updating the Brand Pack itself — every treated surface references these same three files. Currently applied to the closing CTA banner and to creative surfaces only; never to the page surface, cards, buttons, navigation, inputs, small UI, icons, typography or placeholders. Rule: governance/website/rulebooks/visual-language.md §1. Provenance: brand-pack/ASSETS.md.

asset.$description: noise-texture — the final tactile grain that unifies every branded background. Tiled at native grain scale (grain is resolution-relative, not surface-relative).
film-texture — analog tonal variation inspired by scanned film. One composition mapped to the surface. PHOTOGRAPHIC BASES ONLY: never over a solid brand colour.

blend.$description: Blend mode for this layer. `plus-lighter` is valid only on mix-blend-mode.

opacity.$description: Layer opacity. Applies only where the base is a photograph, screenshot, illustration or other creative; a solid-colour surface omits this layer entirely.

asset.$description: grunge-retro-texture — printed imperfection that stops a large colour field reading as digitally flat. Almost imperceptible by design.

opacity.$description: Layer opacity. RECORDED, not declared: pre-applied in the asset's alpha (13/255), because the bottom layer rides the background stack, which has no per-layer opacity.

scrim._comment: THE SCRIM — legibility as a MEASURED property of the surface, not a styling choice. A text-bearing surface carries dark primary text, measured at 6.11:1 against the solid contrast surface. Putting a photograph under that text destroys the measurement: unveiled, the worst case across this library measures 1.02:1 — text that is in practice invisible, and nothing in governance would have caught it, because contrast had only ever been measured against flat colour. So an environment used AS A SURFACE carries a veil of the page cream, and the veil is set by the library's darkest member rather than chosen. Measured on the REAL RENDER — the composite, film and noise and grunge included — the worst asset reads 7.37:1 against the darkest 1% of the editorial column, above the 6.11:1 the solid surface already had. THE SURFACE KEEPS THE MEASUREMENT IT REPLACES. An asset that cannot clear it does not join the library. The veil HOLDS across the editorial column and releases only past it: a straight ramp is already thinning out mid-column and measured 4.45:1, under AA. A creative shown as the SUBJECT is never scrimmed — there is no text to protect, and veiling it would dim the thing being shown.

near.$description: Veil alpha at the alignment edge.

hold.$description: Veil alpha still holding at the end of the editorial column.

far.$description: Veil alpha where the environment breathes past the column.

cream-rgb.$description: The page cream the veil is made of — the same surface the band sits on.

motion._comment: Not an axis this direction covers — left as authored.

instant.$description: Instant — state changes that should not animate.

micro.$description: Micro — tooltips, focus rings, near-instant feedback.

quick.$description: Quick — toggles, hover transitions, button states.

standard.$description: Standard — dropdowns, modal opens, default UI motion.

scene.$description: Scene — a once-per-page reveal. Never on hover.

spring-soft.$description: Toggles, drawers — gentle overshoot then settle.

z-index._comment: Not an axis this direction covers — left as authored. 6-tier stacking.

raised.$description: Deliberate overlap inside a layout — the one z-moment per section.

stroke._comment: One hairline weight, one colour. Avoid heavy borders. With the page held on one surface, hairlines now carry the structural separation that surface switching used to — still punctuation, still sparing.

hairline.$description: The default stroke. One weight throughout.

default.$description: Default stroke width — dividers, cards, inputs, structural separation.

emphasis.$description: Collapsed onto the default. There is no heavy-border tier in this language.

color.$description: DEFAULT focus ring: the primary ink, 13.14:1 on the page ground. NOT downgraded to an accent - blue-500 measures 2.07:1 and fails WCAG 1.4.11. See focus-ring-accent for accent and dark surfaces. DR-24.

color-accent.$description: Focus ring on an accent or dark surface, where a dark ring would disappear. 4.23:1.

breakpoint._comment: Not an axis this direction covers — left as authored. Responsive behaviour is retained; type and spacing scale proportionally across these while preserving the editorial visual language.

sm.$description: Small — large phones, small tablets in portrait.

com.brand-kit.generation.orchestration: single surface; a surface change is a deliberate accent moment, not a rotating band cadence
com.brand-kit.generation.density: spacious — whitespace is the primary mechanism for creating hierarchy
com.brand-kit.generation.radiusVocabulary: two standardized radii: control 6px, large surface 12px
com.brand-kit.generation.shadowPhilosophy: none — no shadows anywhere; hierarchy from spacing, typography, alignment and composition
com.brand-kit.generation.authority: NOT the source of truth. colors_and_type.css is the live value layer; this file is a W3C-shaped export of the same system.
